subject: Budget constraints discovery — pilot ops readout & next-step checklist
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@finsightapp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Budget constraints discovery — pilot ops readout & next-step checklist

Hi Dana — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared view and clear next steps. I captured the things that matter most to you and items where Redwood can help.

Pain points you called out
- Unit/token cost on LLM-powered features (high budget sensitivity for Q4 rollout).
- Occasional 95th pct latency spikes during peak traffic (affects UX and SLOs).
- Limited ops bandwidth: would prefer a small pilot that demonstrates predictable unit economics before expanding.

Current stack / constraints
- Model: in-house distilled LLaMA variant for classification + a hosted general model for fallback.
- Serving today: custom Kubernetes endpoints on GCP with single-GPU VMs, limited batching; no prefix/KV cache reuse.
- Security: standard SOC2 compliance; will share evidence but procurement wants controls scoped.

Success criteria you suggested
- Demonstrate >=30% reduction in per-request token cost for the canonical query mix (classification + short generation).
- 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for <1k QPS simulated pilot load.
- No degradation in model output quality vs. your in-house baseline (we’ll run evals against your gold prompts).

Openness to optimization levers (you said):
- Batching & intelligent routing: high interest.
- Prefix/KV caching: very interested if it preserves latency.
- Quantization: open to trying q4/int8 variants for cost savings under a canary.

Next steps (proposed timeline)
1) We share a short pilot scope doc + MOU (attached: redwood-pilot-scope.pdf) — action: Rafael to send today.
2) You provide a small representative prompt set, ~2–3k queries + traffic profile and a sample of model responses for quality checks — action: Dana to share by EOD Thu 8/20.
3) Redwood sets up a 2-week pilot (dedicated small pool) to run batching, caching, and quantization experiments; we’ll instrument cost/latency traces.
4) Weekly readouts and one final readout with unit-cost comparison and recommended rollout plan.

Logistics / procurement notes
- Procurement will ask for SOC2 and a short data-handling note — I attached SOC2-summary.pdf.
- If the pilot meets success criteria, we can propose a reserved capacity SKU to hit target economics.

If this framing looks right I’ll send the pilot scope + a DocuSign MOU and we can lock in the pilot start next week.

Thanks again — appreciate the candor on tradeoffs, Dana.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@finsightapp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget constraints discovery — pilot ops readout & next-step checklist

Rafael — thanks for the thorough write-up. This aligns well. A few clarifications and one ask from procurement: 

Clarifications
- For success criteria: the 30% reduction target is relative to our monthly token spend for the classification service (roughly $18k/month today).
- Latency target: 95th <= 250ms is acceptable; for baseline we can provide logs for the last 30 days.
- Quantization: happy to run canaries but we need to see accuracy delta on our gold set.

Procurement ask
- They want a short (1 page) statement that data ingested for the pilot will not be used to train models and will be deleted after 90 days unless we execute a contract. Can you provide that?

We’ll share the prompt set and 2k sample queries by Thursday. Also attaching current infra diagram (finsight-current-architecture.png) in the Drive link you provided.

Thanks — Dana
Dana Ruiz
Head of Platform, FinSight
dana.ruiz@finsightapp.com

Attachment references: finsight-current-architecture.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget constraints discovery — pilot ops readout & next-step checklist

Quick internal note / ops checklist before we turn the MOU: 
- Rafael: I’ll draft the pilot config for the small dedicated pool (2x A10-equivalent) and include batching/caching knobs + a quantization branch.
- Marissa: can you prefill the pricing comparison template with the FS baseline spend (Dana said ~$18k/month) — we’ll model 3 scenarios (no-opt, batching/caching, batching+caching+q4).
- I’ll also draft the procurement one-pager on data usage and retention (explicit: no training, 90-day retention, KMS encryption in transit and at rest).

We should be ready to send the MOU by EOD today once Rafael confirms the scope doc.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dana — thanks, will do. Short answers: 
- Data statement: yes — we’ll provide the one-page confirmation (no training, 90-day deletion, encrypted) in the MOU. Aditya is drafting the language now.
- Pilot scope: attached redwood-pilot-scope.pdf (lightweight MOU + objectives).
- Timeline: if we get your sample set by Thu 8/20 we can start the pilot the week of 8/24 and read out by 9/7.

Action items summarized:
- Dana: share prompt set + traffic profile by Thu 8/20 (procurement included).
- Aditya: pilot config + procurement one-pager (today).
- Marissa: run initial unit-cost model and share a comparison table in the pilot doc (Mon 8/24).

If that works I’ll send the DocuSign and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Rafael
